commits.message: [Phase 0] Optimize step loop: numpy rollout + param stack cache + jnp.asarray in PPO
commits.body:
Three per-step performance improvements (no behavioral change):

1. Rollout buffer now uses NumPy arrays instead of JAX. Each step previously
   called buf.at[ptr].set() (creates a new JAX array) for 4 fields × n_agents.
   NumPy in-place assignment is ~20x faster (~1ms vs ~23ms at 45 agents).
   ppo_update calls jnp.asarray() at the start to convert before JAX ops.

2. Stacked policy params cache (_get_stacked_params / _update_param_slot).
   Previously rebuilt jtu.tree_map stack from scratch every step (~51ms).
   Now cached by agent-id tuple; rebuilt only when births/deaths occur.
   After PPO update, only the changed agent's slot is updated via .at[].set().
   Saves ~50ms on the ~99% of steps with no population change.

3. Removed redundant get_observation + policy_forward in PPO trigger.
   The computed last_value was discarded anyway (ppo.py hardcodes last_value=0.0).

Result: 317ms/step → ~116ms/step measured at 45 agents (~8.6 steps/s in
isolated benchmark); 4.4 steps/s measured in full loop at 87 agents (step 5000).
25k smoke test projected ~1.5-2h vs original ~6h estimate.

- tests/test_checkpoint_jax.py: 9 tests covering roundtrip, atomic

commits.body:

--xla_cpu_enable_fast_math and --xla_cpu_use_thunk_runtime. Flags are

  Before: 7.0 steps/s (pre-PPO, 500 steps, --runtime mac.yaml)
  After:  9.8 steps/s (same run)

and stds) are identical at the displayed precision — fast-math's
sub-ULP numerical differences don't affect anything we care about
at the scale of this workload.

commits.body:

to determine where real time goes when sim_step_core runs slow.

Key finding from running this on Mac at 198 agents (M4 Pro, fast-math):
  physics (phyjax2d)        72.3% of step time
  energy + births + food    19.5%
  observations               7.2%
  eating (O(N^2) catch)      0.5%  ← was suspected bottleneck; isn't
  policy sample              0.5%

commits.message: [Perf] Batch the per-step PPO readiness check (29% Mac speedup)
commits.body:
Previously the runner called np.array(sim_state.rollout_ptrs) every
step, which blocks the Python loop waiting for GPU/CPU to finish
sim_step_core. Now we only check readiness every PPO_CHECK_EVERY steps
(default 10, overridable via EVO_PPO_CHECK_EVERY env var).

Measured on Mac M4 Pro (fast-math enabled), 2000 steps, seed 0,
--runtime mac.yaml:

  K=1  (old behavior): 2.1 steps/s
  K=10 (new default):  2.7 steps/s     ~29% faster

On L4 GPU the sync cost is larger, so the win is likely ≥ 29%. Have
not re-benchmarked on GPU (that's $0.70/hr) but will observe the rate
on the real Phase 1a run.

Correctness tradeoff: when an agent's rollout fills (ptrs hits
rollout_steps=1024), subsequent sim_step_core calls clip the write
index to slot 1023 (src/jax_sim.py:123) — so the final slot may be
overwritten by up to (PPO_CHECK_EVERY - 1) later observations before
PPO fires. At K=10 and rollout_steps=1024 that's 0.1% of the rollout
being 1-9 steps "late" per update.

Empirically at step 2000, K=1 vs K=10 gives:
  prey=244 vs 243, pred=23 vs 24 (within normal stochastic variance)
  w_pred mean: -0.04 vs -0.05 (both show fear direction)
  w_prey mean: +0.00 vs +0.00 (identical at 2-decimal precision)

Well within seed-to-seed variance. Set EVO_PPO_CHECK_EVERY=1 to
recover exact-timing baseline for comparison runs.

Final-flush safety: _maybe_fire_ppo is also called before each
checkpoint write and once more at the end of the run, so saved state
always reflects a post-PPO-sweep view (no stale in-progress
rollouts).

All 141 tests still pass (tests call sim_step_core directly and
are unaffected by the runner-side batching).

commits.message: [Infra] spot_orchestrator: auto-create NAT + SSH retry with backoff
commits.body:
Two reliability fixes after the first run failed on us-west1-a:

1. Each region needs its own Cloud NAT (NAT is regional). The
   orchestrator now calls ensure_nat(zone) right after a successful
   VM create, checking for the router/NAT in the VM's region and
   creating them if missing. Idempotent — no-ops when they exist.

2. Fresh VMs aren't ready for SSH for ~30-90s after create (ssh key
   propagation, sshd startup). wait_for_ssh() polls with backoff
   (30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180s — up to ~7 min of patience) before
   handing off to provision().

No behavior change when things work; just way more tolerant of the
normal transient failures of GCP spot capacity handoff.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] Preemption-hardened orchestrator via GCP startup-script
commits.body:
Previous orchestrator installed apt packages + jax[cuda12] via SSH
from the laptop. That took 10-15 minutes during which the spot VM
was especially vulnerable to preemption, and mid-install preemption
killed SSH and the orchestrator exited.

New architecture:

- scripts/vm_startup.sh: idempotent bootstrap script passed as
  instance metadata. Runs as root on every VM boot (including after
  spot preemption + restart). Installs apt packages, creates venv,
  installs jax[cuda12]. If repo + phase1a_loop.sh have been uploaded,
  also installs requirements and starts the tmux training session.
  Logs to /var/log/evo-startup.log. Writes /tmp/evo-ready once the
  base env is ready.

- scripts/spot_orchestrator.py rewritten as a reconcile-loop:
  1. Get (or poll for) a zone with spot capacity; create VM with
     vm_startup.sh as startup-script metadata.
  2. Each cycle, describe the VM and drive it to the target state:
     TERMINATED -> start; RUNNING -> wait for ready marker; then
     upload repo + loop script if missing; then start tmux if missing.
  3. Every step is idempotent and failure-tolerant. No step ever
     calls sys.exit — failures just leave the cycle incomplete and
     the next iteration retries.
  4. On preemption restart, vm_startup.sh restarts the tmux session
     automatically; the orchestrator just has to notice RUNNING.

Wait windows:
  * wait_for_ssh: up to 6 min for sshd + key propagation
  * wait_for_ready_marker: up to 30 min for jax[cuda12] install to
    finish on first boot (it's ~500MB of CUDA wheels)

State is still in .claude-orch-state.json so rerunning picks up the
existing VM.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] spot_orchestrator: detect preemption mid-wait, faster reconcile
commits.body:
Two fixes after observing the orchestrator stuck in a 30-min wait
loop while the VM was already TERMINATED:

1. wait_for_ready_marker polls VM status each iteration and returns
   False immediately if status != RUNNING. The outer reconcile loop
   then restarts the VM on the next cycle.

2. READY_MARKER_ATTEMPTS dropped from 60 (30 min) to 10 (5 min).
   Longer install progress naturally spans multiple reconcile cycles
   since the startup-script is idempotent — no reason to hold one
   cycle open for 30 min while pretending nothing is wrong.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] GCS-backed checkpoints + persistent-stockout fallback
commits.body:
Two fixes that together make the spot orchestrator survive sustained
GCP capacity pressure:

1. GCS-backed checkpoints (cross-zone recovery).
   vm_startup.sh now reads instance-metadata key `gcs-bucket` and:
     - on boot, `gsutil rsync` from gs://$BUCKET/results -> local
       (restores a new VM to the last saved state of the previous VM)
     - starts a tmux session that pushes local results -> GCS every
       5 min (incremental, survives preemption)
   The orchestrator creates the bucket on startup, attaches it via
   metadata to each VM, and gives the VM cloud-platform scope so its
   default service account can read/write.

2. Persistent-stockout fallback (delete+recreate elsewhere).
   After 3 consecutive stockout failures on `instances start` in the
   same zone (~15 min), the orchestrator deletes the stuck VM and
   polls all zones for fresh capacity. With GCS-backed checkpoints
   in place, the new VM pulls prior results before resuming training —
   minimal progress loss.

This unblocks the case we just hit: us-central1-a preempted our VM
and then refused to restart it due to stockout. Before these fixes
the orchestrator would loop forever on same-zone retry. After these
fixes, new VM in an available zone with checkpoints restored.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] spot_orchestrator: --on-demand flag instead of auto-fallback
commits.body:
The decision of when to abandon spot is a user judgment, not an
orchestrator policy. Replaced the time-based auto-fallback with an
explicit --on-demand flag.

Usage: when spot capacity is chronically bad and you'd rather pay
the premium for certainty, kill the spot orchestrator and re-run:

    python3 scripts/spot_orchestrator.py --on-demand --seed 0

Everything else stays identical — same state file, same GCS
checkpoint bucket, same reconcile loop. The new VM just skips the
--provisioning-model=SPOT / termination-action flags, so it's a
regular on-demand VM that won't be preempted.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] Line-buffer runner stdout so phase1a.log updates in real time
commits.body:
Without unbuffered output, Python's stdout piped through tee sat in
a ~4KB block buffer. On a real Phase 1a run the first log line at
step 5000 emits about 150 bytes, so nothing appeared in phase1a.log
for many minutes while training was quietly running on the GPU. Made
it look like training was hung when it was actually fine.

Fix: wrap the runner with stdbuf -oL -eL python -u, and pipe through
stdbuf -oL tee, forcing line-buffering end to end. Progress lines now
appear in phase1a.log within seconds of being printed.

Only the orchestrator-generated phase1a_loop.sh script was changed;
tests and repo code are untouched.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Tools] status.py monitoring dashboard + docs/monitoring.md
commits.body:
Goal: day-to-day operations of the GCP Phase 1a run should never
require remembering raw gcloud commands or manually tailing logs.

- scripts/status.py: one-shot status CLI. Reads the orchestrator

  the last lines of phase1a.log, parses the latest progress line
  (Step N/M | prey=... | w_pred=... | ...), and renders a compact
  color-coded dashboard: VM status, provisioning model, training
  progress, ETA, GPU utilization, population counts, reward-weight
  means (with green indicators when fear + affiliation are
  emerging in the right direction), retry count, and the
  canonical tail-log / tmux-attach commands footer. --follow N
  refreshes in place every N seconds.

- tests/test_status.py: 10 unit tests for the log-line regex + the
  format helpers. Pure-function coverage; subprocess / gcloud paths
  are validated live.

- docs/monitoring.md: tools at a glance, quick-reference one-liners,
  status dashboard walkthrough, lifecycle operations (start /
  resume / on-demand switch / teardown), and a troubleshooting
  section with the failure modes we hit during this session.

- README.md: link to the new monitoring doc alongside gcp-setup
  and gcp-spot.

Full test suite: 161 passed + 3 skipped (was 151 + 3).

commits.message: [Config] Shorten spot checkpoint interval: 25k -> 10k steps
commits.body:
Four spot VM attempts today lost 100% of training progress because
every preemption happened before the first checkpoint was written.
Checkpoint interval was 25k steps (~12 min at 34 sps), but measured
preemption window during contested capacity is ~10-15 min. Shortening
to 10k (~5 min wall clock) lets us survive typical preemptions —
several checkpoints land before the VM is reclaimed, so new VMs
resume from GCS instead of starting from step 0.

Save overhead goes from ~3% to ~5-7% of wall clock, which is still
much cheaper than the total-progress-loss we'd been eating.

If spot capacity remains chronically bad, on-demand (via
--on-demand on spot_orchestrator.py) stays a clean off-ramp.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] orchestrator: surface actual gcloud error instead of assuming stockout
commits.body:
Prior behavior: any failed `gcloud compute instances create` was logged
as "trying <zone>..." with no follow-up, so quota errors, permission
problems, and all other non-capacity failures were invisibly rolled
up as "stockout, sleeping 10min".

Hit this today when 200GB orphan disks pushed us past SSD_TOTAL_GB
quota in us-central1 — orchestrator reported "all zones stockout"
but the real error was quota, fixable in seconds by deleting the
stuck disk.

Now each failed create logs a one-line summary (stockout, SSD quota,
general quota, permissions, already-exists, or the last line of
gcloud's error).
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Infra] orchestrator: start gcs-sync sidecar directly, not via startup-script
commits.body:
vm_startup.sh only launched the gcs-sync tmux session if the repo was
already on disk when it ran. But the orchestrator uploads the repo
AFTER the startup-script has finished its first pass — so gcs-sync
was never launched on a fresh VM, which meant local checkpoints
never synced to GCS. Local disk is durable for on-demand VMs, but
we lose our cross-zone safety net for spot, and there's no backup
against accidental VM deletion for either mode.

Fix: start both phase1a AND gcs-sync tmux sessions from the
orchestrator's start_tmux() step, which runs after the repo is
guaranteed to be in place. Idempotent — if gcs-sync is already
running, it's left alone.

Also reported in the orchestrator log output now, so a missing
gcs-sync is immediately visible.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Docs] Add K&D 2024/2025 arXiv .tex sources for LLM-readable reference
commits.body:
LLM agents can now grep the actual paper text directly instead of

commits.message: [Tools] status.py: hardcode project/account + retry on TERMINATED
commits.body:
Two fixes after status.py returned wildly wrong data (reported a VM
as TERMINATED in spot mode when it was actually RUNNING on-demand):

1. Pin CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT and CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT as env vars
   for every gcloud subprocess call. If the user's shell-global
   gcloud config points at a different project (as likely happened
   since they maintain another project for unrelated work), we were
   querying the wrong thing and silently getting back a same-named
   VM from that project. Now status.py is safe to run from any
   terminal without sourcing scripts/gcloud-env.sh first.

2. Retry once with a 2s delay if describe returns TERMINATED. GCP
   describe is eventually-consistent and very occasionally returns
   stale state. A single retry smooths over transient blips; a
   genuinely TERMINATED VM stays TERMINATED on the second call so
   real outages still surface.

Usage unchanged:
  python3 scripts/status.py
  python3 scripts/status.py --follow 30

All 10 tests still pass.

commits.message: [Docs] Record April 2026 spot experience + on-demand as the default
commits.body:
After a multi-hour attempt to run Phase 1a seed 0 on GCP spot L4
VMs that kept getting preempted within 10-15 min of creation (before
any checkpoint could land in GCS), we fell back to on-demand. This
commit captures the lessons so future runs start with the right
expectations.

- docs/gcp-spot.md: new "⚠ When spot works — and when it doesn't"
  admonition at the top, plus an updated caveat to the cost table
  noting that contested-capacity runs can cost more than on-demand
  if every attempt ends in preemption without forward progress.

- docs/monitoring.md: expanded troubleshooting with two new
  sections — "SSD quota exceeded" (the error the orchestrator used
  to mask as stockout, fixed in a previous commit; now this is the
  user-facing playbook when it happens) and "Telling if spot isn't
  going to work" (concrete decision signals + the one-liner to
  switch modes). GCS-backed checkpoints from prior spot attempts
  carry over, so the switch is non-destructive.

- README.md: note on the gcp-spot link that on-demand is the default
  recommendation; try spot only when capacity is healthy.

No code changes — the spot path stays intact as a one-flag option
for future runs when the GCP L4 market is less contested.

commits.message: [Docs+Validation] Apply K&D audit corrections across docs and gate criteria
commits.body:

Pipeline:

    training loop, captures only inside the window leading up to each
    flush boundary (zero cost outside). Quantizes positions to uint16

  scripts/replay_upload.py    — upload, list, delete, index rebuild on

commits.message: [Fix] D18 — predator feeding mechanics bundle
commits.body:
Phase 1a seed 0 on GCP ran for 1.67M steps with predator reward
weights IDENTICAL TO 3 DECIMAL PLACES for the last ~1M. Root cause:
predators saturated at energy cap (999/1000) and the K&D hazard
function vanishes at high energy (exp(-β_h·1000) = rounding-error
zero), so predators were literally immortal. No deaths → no slot
turnover → mutated offspring never entered the population → reward
genome frozen at initialization.

Why they saturated: TWO bugs in our catch mechanic, plus THREE
config-value drifts discovered while cross-checking emevo TOMLs
(gecco2026 branch).

Fixes (bundled per user request):

1. Cooldown (SimState.predator_eat_timer). Mirrors emevo's
   predator_eat_timer countdown: resets to predator_eat_interval=10
   on a catch, decrements each step otherwise. Predator can only
   catch when timer <= 0.

2. Catch geometry (jax_food.py::check_eating_jax).
   OLD (buggy):  dist in [40, 80] AND angle within ±30° of heading
   NEW (emevo):  dist <= pred_radius + prey_radius (physical contact)
                 AND nearest tactile bin in predator_mouth_tactile_bins
                 (default [0, 1, 17] = 60° front arc)

3. beta_b = 0.1 → 0.4 (emevo: slope = 0.4 for both species).
   Shifts peak birth rate from energy cap (e~1000) to moderate
   energies (e~250 for predator with ζ=100).

4. zeta_b_prey = 10 → 15 (emevo delay = 15 in prey bd config).
   Raises the half-max birth energy for prey.

5. beta_t_prey = 2e-6 → 4e-6 (emevo beta = 4e-6 in prey bd config).
   Prey age-dependent hazard was half emevo's scale; prey were
   living ~2x too long.

Source references in emevo (gecco2026 branch):
  * src/emevo/environments/circle_foraging_with_predator.py — step,
    _collect_tactile, predator_eat_timer update
  * config/env/20251122-predator-square.toml — env params
  * config/bd/20240916-sel-a4e7-d15.toml — prey birth/death
  * config/bd/20241229-predator-d100.toml — predator birth/death

Validation:
  * 170/170 tests pass (including 7 new tests in test_predator_eating.py
    pinning contact + bin + cooldown semantics)
  * Local 3000-step smoke: mean energy stabilizes at ~86 (not 1000);
    reward weights visibly move (w_pred for prey: 0 -> -0.05; w_eat
    for predator: 0 -> -0.70); births + deaths happen (population
    hits caps naturally via turnover); no immortal-predator pattern.
  * Checkpoint incompatibility: the new SimState has an extra
    predator_eat_timer field; old checkpoints from the buggy run
    fail to load (intentional — they represented invalid training).
    GCS bucket wiped; restart from scratch.

commits.message: [D19] Slot↔body fix + phyjax2d contact plumbing + invariant tests
commits.body:
After D18 (D18: contact + mouth-bin + cooldown) Phase 1a still saw
only 1 birth per 70K steps. Root cause was two coupled bugs:

1. Slot mismatch: init_simstate placed predators contiguously after
   prey (slots n_prey..n_prey+n_pred-1), but _build_physics reserves
   slots [0, prey_cap) for prey-radius bodies and [prey_cap, max_agents)
   for predator-radius bodies. Our "predators" lived in prey-sized
   bodies — wrong mass, wrong inertia, smaller collision surface.

2. Post-step distance check missed mid-step contacts. phyjax2d's
   velocity solver separates colliders during substeps; by step-end
   the distance rarely showed contact even when the two circles
   clearly touched during some substep.

Fix mirrors emevo gecco2026 circle_foraging.py::nstep:
  * Species-reserved slots: prey [0, prey_cap), predator [prey_cap, max)
  * Birth dispatcher finds free slot in parent's species range
  * physics_step emits contact.penetration >= 0 per substep,
    reduces via jnp.max(axis=0)
  * sim_step_core calls space.get_contact_mat("circle", "circle", ...)
    to build (A, A) bool matrix, passes to check_eating_jax
  * check_eating_jax uses contact_mat instead of distance check

Tests: +21 new (17 fast + 4 slow), 182 total passing. Covers the
slot↔body invariant, species-correct births, param drift vs emevo
TOML, and short-dynamics smoke (catches + turnover + no energy
saturation). Updates existing test fixtures to the new layout.

pins added at 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k, 150k, 300k for early-coverage.

  results/<exp>/seed_<N>/<run_tag>/{checkpoints,replays,progress.json,metrics.npz}

`run_tag` resolution (--run-tag | --run-name flags on the runner):
  - fresh run: UTC timestamp '2026-04-21T1447Z' (+ optional _<name> suffix)
  - --resume: auto-picks the latest existing tag for the seed; falls back
    to legacy untagged layout if no tagged runs exist
  - --run-tag '' explicitly: legacy untagged layout (back-compat)

GCS replay uploads already supported `run_tag` (introduced for the
pre-D18 vs current comparison); this wires the CLI value through the
ReplayRecorder so each run's milestones land under its own tag.

Retention is now scoped to (exp, seed, run_tag) so one run's
milestone-pruning pass can't evict another run's replays from the
shared public bucket.

Side benefit: replay local path was double-nested before
(results/<exp>/seed_<N>/replays/<exp>/seed_<N>/step_<S>/); the new
layout flattens to results/<exp>/seed_<N>/<run_tag>/replays/step_<S>/.

commits.message: [D20] Deactivate caught prey + verify_replay.py integrity check
commits.body:
Found while building a post-hoc replay verifier: even after D18+D19,
predators showed 0 catches counted as deaths, saturated at ~991 energy,
and populations stayed pinned at cap for 10K-step windows. Root cause:
check_eating_jax was producing pred_catch_slots but nothing ever
deactivated those prey. Predators harvested +eta*prey_energy on the
catch, the prey kept existing, and the 10-step cooldown let the same
pair pairwise-feed the predator forever. Predator cost < gain → cap.

Fix: check_eating_jax now also returns prey_caught_mask (A,) bool, and
sim_step_core applies a same-step deactivation right after eating-check
— clears is_active, zeroes energy, resets rollout ptr, and turns off
the physics body / velocity — mirroring the death path already in
process_births_and_deaths_jax. The fix is a 15-line addition; no
reward / energy / physics math changed.

Local 2K-step smoke with tiny config (30 prey cap, 10 pred cap):
  pre-D20: pred mean_energy ≈ 991 (cap 1000), 0 births after init
  post-D20: pred mean_energy = 87.5, 11 births past initial 25 slots

Added tests/test_sim_dynamics.py::test_caught_prey_actually_die and
test_predator_energy_not_saturated_at_5k as regression guards.
Full suite: 193 passed (was 189).

Also adds scripts/verify_replay.py, a post-hoc integrity check:
downloads a replay from the public GCS bucket (or reads local),
counts frame-pair events (feedings, catches, births, deaths),
reports predator energy band, and flags obvious pathologies. This
is what surfaced D20 — running it against the in-flight "post-D19"
replay showed 0 catches / saturated energy / 0 deaths, which no
amount of D18+D19 math could explain.

commits.message: [D20 self-fix + D21 visibility] + audit findings
commits.body:
Three related fixes plus a visibility pass to catch future silent-
correctness bugs within one log interval instead of one replay flush.

── D20 self-fix (BLOCKER from last commit b39d084) ──────────────────
The previous D20 patch zeroed caught prey energies right before
update_energies_jax read them, so predators got pred_gain = eta * 0 = 0
on every catch and slowly starved. Verified end-to-end via a new
test (TestEnergyTransfer::test_predator_energy_jumps_after_catch):
place a predator touching a prey with E=80, run one sim step, assert
predator energy went up by ≈ eta*80 − metabolic cost. Fix: drop the
energies-zeroing line; leaving caught prey's energy on the inactive
slot is harmless (all downstream reads are is_active-masked) and
keeps update_energies_jax's +eta*E transfer working.

── Audit Finding 2: reset predator_eat_timer on rebirth ──────────────
spawn_offspring_jax was writing ~20 slot fields but not
predator_eat_timer, so a newborn could inherit a dead parent's stale
countdown (e.g. timer=9 → unable to catch for 9 steps after birth).
Moderate severity — skews selection against successful lineages.
New test: TestSpawnOffspring::test_child_predator_eat_timer_reset.

── Latent: birth scan axis mismatch for tiny configs ─────────────────
process_births_and_deaths_jax's lax.scan over max_births_per_step=20
failed when max_agents < 20 (jnp.sort(...)[:20] returns max_agents
elements, not 20). Only visible in unit tests, but padding the sort
output to a fixed 20 is a trivial defensive fix.

── D21: per-interval event counters + energy bands + warnings ────────
SimState gains three int32 counters (cum_catches, cum_deaths,
cum_feedings) that tick inside sim_step_core / births-deaths. The
runner diffs them between log intervals to produce per-interval
event counts. progress.json gains two new blocks:

  events_last_interval: {catches, deaths, births, feedings, interval_steps}
  energy_stats: {prey: {min,mean,max}, pred: {min,mean,max}}

The Step text log now includes the delta counts and per-species energy
bands, and prints one-line ⚠ warnings when:
  * no catches across 2 consecutive log intervals
  * no births across 5 consecutive log intervals
  * min(pred energy) > energy_capacity * 0.95 (saturation)

Storage cost: ~3 extra int32 in SimState (12B), ~300 bytes more per
progress.json write. Negligible even at 100K-interval cadence over
10.24M steps.

Full suite: 195 passed (was 193 — two new tests added here).

Local 3K-step smoke on small config shows healthy dynamics:
  before D20 self-fix:  predators starve, population collapses to 10
  after:  cum_catches=2, cum_deaths=2, pred energy mean=87
          (balanced), 32 births past initial

Adds two new red_flags:
  * PREY_EXTINCTION_RISK when prey drops below 30 in a window
    (K&D §4.2 steady state is ~349, so < 30 is ~10x below and

commits.message: [D22] Paper-text alignment: beta_t_prey, zeta_b_prey, food_radius
commits.body:
Cross-check of the K&D 2025 paper (arXiv 2507.09992v2, Feb 2026) against
the emevo gecco2026 endpoint (experiments/cf_predator.py) surfaced that
paper text and endpoint code disagree on 5 parameters. Our config
matched endpoint defaults on 3 of these (β_t_prey=4e-6, ζ_b_prey=15,
using distance threshold prey_radius only for food contact). That
combination produced prey extinction at step 90K in phase1a-v2.

Chose to match paper text over endpoint code for three reasons:
  1. Appendix A explicitly states "square 960×960" (we already match)
  2. Fig 19 (birth function plot) shows prey saturation at e≈25-30,
     consistent only with ζ=10, not ζ=15
  3. Paper text "30 energy units are required for prey birth"
     matches ζ=10 saturation

Three changes:
  * configs/baseline_faithful.yaml:
    - beta_t_prey: 4e-6 → 2e-6 (paper Table 3)
    - zeta_b_prey: 15 → 10 (paper Table 3 + Fig 19)
    - Add food_radius: 4.0 (paper App A + emevo code)
  * src/jax_food.py::check_eating_jax:
    - Contact threshold: dist ≤ prey_radius → dist ≤ prey_radius +
      food_radius = 14. Matches emevo's physics-engine contact_mat
      (circle-circle contact uses r1+r2). Pre-D22 we had effective
      contact area = (10/14)² = 51% of emevo's, which compounded
      with the lower birth rate to starve prey.
  * tests/test_params_match_emevo.py pins the new values plus a grep
    that check_eating_jax uses food_radius.

Also adds configs/baseline_endpoint.yaml preserving the endpoint-code
parameterization (1200×600 rect, 9 tactile bins, 160° FOV, β=4e-6,
ζ=15) for later experimentation. NOT YET RUNNABLE — needs rectangular-
world + variable-tactile-bin support; documented as TODO at file top.

Full fast suite: 185 passed (was 184; +1 new regression test).

commits.message: [D23] Mark rollout_dones=True on agent death (semantic fix)
commits.body:
PPO audit surfaced that sim_step_core writes rollout_dones=False
unconditionally every step, even when an agent dies that step. GAE
then bootstraps past terminal transitions instead of masking them.

Severity is cosmetic in the current architecture (PPO's is_active
gate prevents dead-agent rollouts from being consumed and rebirth
zeros the buffer), so this is NOT the predator-extinction blocker.
But the flag is semantically required and future-proofs any change
that relaxes the PPO gate.

Two-part fix:
  * sim_step_core step 6: rollout_dones write takes prey_caught_mask
    instead of hard-coded False. D20 catches now flip done=True at
    the prey's last rollout slot.
  * process_births_and_deaths_jax: new kwarg rollout_ptrs_for_done
    (= safe_ptrs used in step 6) drives an OR-merge of dead_mask
    into rollout_dones at each dying agent's last rollout slot.
    Handles hazard/starvation deaths too.

Regression test:
  tests/test_predator_eating.py::TestDoneFlagOnDeath
  Places a predator touching a prey in the mouth arc, runs one full
  sim_step_core, asserts rollout_dones[prey, old_ptr] == True.

Fast suite: 186 passed (was 185).

Extinction at step 80K persists in isolation — the PPO audit ruled
out other plumbing issues, so next-session's priority is either the
endpoint-code refactor (rectangular world + 9 tactile bins) or
another round of audit in yet-unexplored territory.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [D24] Energy cost uses act_ratio-scaled action norm
commits.body:
Physics/observations audit surfaced that emevo's force_norm for the
energy-cost formula is derived from post-act_ratio scaled force,
while ours used the raw policy action. For predators,
act_ratio = (pred_r/prey_r)² = 1.96, so our code was undercharging
predator energy cost by ~49% (not the other direction — the audit's
impact diagnosis was reversed).

Fix is in src/jax_lifecycle.py::update_energies_jax:
  scaled_actions = all_actions * sim_state.act_ratio
  action_norms = jnp.linalg.norm(scaled_actions, axis=1)

Reward motor_norm (in src/jax_sim.py) stays on raw actions — that's
correct and matches emevo's SensorActFoodExtractor.normalize_action,
which calls act_space.sigmoid_scale(action) without act_ratio.

Regression test: tests/test_predator_eating.py::TestEnergyCostScaling
feeds the same raw (50, 50) action to a prey and a predator at
matched starting energy and asserts predator drain > 10× prey drain.
Can only hold if act_ratio is applied.

NOT expected to fix extinction (in fact tilts slightly against
predators), but removes a genuine semantic mismatch with emevo and
narrows the remaining unknowns.

Full fast suite: 187 passed (was 186).
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [D25] Rectangular world support (+ make baseline_endpoint runnable)
commits.body:
Our code assumed a square world via `world_size` as a scalar. Emevo's
cf_predator.py endpoint defaults to 1200×600 rectangular (via
20241212-predator.toml). Our paper-faithful config uses 960×960 square
and has been hitting predator extinction; we want the option to test
the endpoint parameterization without rewriting every call site.

Added: src/environment.py::world_bounds(config) -> tuple[float, float]
with three-way back-compat:
  * world_size_x + world_size_y → explicit rectangle
  * world_size = [x, y] → tuple in the scalar field
  * world_size = N → legacy scalar (square) — returns (N, N)

Threaded (world_x, world_y) through every scalar-world_size site in
the JAX path: _build_physics, init_simstate (positions + food),
regenerate_food_jax, spawn_offspring_jax, _compute_wall_distances,
_single_tactile. phyjax2d's `make_square_segments` already supports
rectangles (the name is misleading); emevo calls it the same way.

configs/baseline_endpoint.yaml now runs end-to-end through
sim_step_core. Its "NOT YET RUNNABLE" header comment is stale for
the world/position plumbing (fixed here) but still applies to
tactile mouth-range string decoding ("front-wide" / "narrow"),
which is low-severity; our FOV check is functionally similar.

Regression suite (tests/test_rectangular_world.py, 10 new tests):
  * world_bounds resolution for all three config shapes
  * endpoint config bounds, initial positions, food positions all
    fall inside [0, 1200] × [0, 600] AND hit the long axis (no
    accidental clamping to the smaller dimension)
  * sim_step_core runs 5 steps end-to-end on the endpoint config
  * paper-faithful config still resolves to (960, 960); population
    count unchanged after init (additive-only for square worlds)

Full fast suite: 197 passed (was 187).

Not a deviation from emevo. Emevo supports square (xlim=ylim) and
rectangle (xlim≠ylim) via the same API. We now match that shape.

commits.message: [D26] Tactile bin indexing off by 90° — fix mouth arc + tactile obs
commits.body:
TL;DR: the most likely root cause of predator extinction.

phyjax2d/emevo convention: agent heading=0 means forward=+y (not +x).
phyjax2d's get_relative_angle subtracts an extra π/2 when mapping a
world-frame angle into the agent's local frame. Our code omitted that
offset in both check_eating_jax and _single_tactile.

Observed effect:
  * predator_mouth_tactile_bins = [0, 1, 17] (60° front arc per K&D)
    actually pointed 90° to the predator's RIGHT side. Predators
    physically could not catch prey directly in front of them.
  * _single_tactile didn't even take obs_angle — tactile observations
    were in world frame, so "bin 0" varied with the agent's heading,
    preventing stable policy learning on tactile inputs.

Verified concretely: predator at (500, 500) heading=0, prey at
(500, 520) — directly in front per phyjax2d convention. Pre-D26 our
code classified this into bin 5 (center 100° = right side). emevo
classifies the same geometry into bin 0.

Fix (src/jax_food.py + src/observations.py):
  rel = (angle_world - obs_angle - π/2) % 2π     # [0, 2π)
  bin = floor(rel / (2π / n_bins))
Extracted _bin_in_agent_frame helper for shared use across
catch detection + tactile obs (agents, food, walls).

FP subtlety: emevo uses (... + 3·TWO_PI - π/2) % TWO_PI, but in fp32
the +3·TWO_PI introduces rounding that snaps rel=0 to near-TWO_PI
(putting "directly in front" into bin n-1). JAX's `%` returns
non-negative for positive divisors, so we drop the extra offset.

Also updated the pre-JAX Python reference compute_tactile_sensors in
src/environment.py to match the convention so the legacy vs JAX
comparison tests (test_vectorized_obs.py) stay green.

Tests added (tests/test_tactile_bin_indexing.py, 6 tests):
  - prey directly in front (+y from heading=0) → bin 0 → caught
  - prey at world +x with heading=0 → bin 13 → NOT in mouth → NOT caught
    (pre-D26 this would have been incorrectly caught — the bug signature)
  - directly-in-front catch works for 8 different headings 0°-315°
  - tactile obs agrees with catch pipeline's convention
  - tactile bin rotates with observer heading (not world-fixed)

Existing predator-eating tests updated to use the correct convention:
previous tests placed prey at +x calling it "east/in front" (which
matched the old broken convention); new placements put prey at +y
relative to heading=0 so "in front" is actually in front.

Full fast suite: 203 passed (was 197; +6 new tests).
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Tests] Paper-anchored test suite (14 tests)
commits.body:
Tests whose assertions quote EXTERNAL sources (K&D 2025 paper sections,
phyjax2d source comments, emevo TOMLs) rather than our own code. Design
rule: each test's docstring cites its anchor, so 'baking in our
assumptions' is explicit — if our implementation drifts from the paper,
these break against the paper quote.

Categories:

  1. Convention pinning (3 tests) — phyjax2d heading=0 means forward=+y,
     bin 0 is the forward arc boundary, local +y force produces world
     velocity in (−sin θ, cos θ). Would have caught D26 directly.

  2. Transformation invariants (3 tests) — catch outcome rotation-
     invariant, translation-invariant, sim_step deterministic under
     same RNG. D26's 90°-off mouth broke rotation invariance.

  3. Fuzz invariants (2 tests) — prey directly behind predator never
     caught across 25 random (heading, position, distance) cases;
     cumulative counters monotone across 50 steps.

  4. Paper-claim tests (6 tests) — predator catch gain ~ eta·prey_e
     (paper Section 3 'gain 6-10 energy units per predation'), prey
     birth threshold near e=30 (Section 3 '30 energy required'),
     predator birth threshold near e=260, initial populations 150/10
     match Section 4, world bounds 960×960 match Appendix A.

Paper-claim tests use a separate paper_config fixture that loads the
real baseline_faithful.yaml rather than the shrunk test fixture — so a
param regression (zeta, beta_t, world_size, initial counts) in the
real config fails here immediately.

commits.message: [Tools] scripts/trace_agent.py — post-hoc per-agent trace
commits.body:
Loads a SimState checkpoint and runs sim_step_core forward for N steps,
recording everything ONE specific agent experienced along the way.
Because the simulation is deterministic (rng_key lives on SimState),
replaying from a checkpoint reproduces the original run bit-for-bit —
no training-time instrumentation needed, no ongoing storage cost.

Per step the trace logs: position, angle, velocity, energy, age,
action, log_prob, value, reward, done, is_active, plus snapshots of
the global cum_catches / cum_deaths / cum_feedings counters. Action /
reward / log_prob / value are read from the rollout buffer after each
step (sim_step_core just wrote them at rollout_ptrs[slot] - 1), so
there's no code duplication of the step logic.

Size budget:
  * thin (no obs):       ~50 B/step     →  10K steps ≈ 500 KB
  * --include-obs:       ~870 B/step    →  10K steps ≈ 8.6 MB

Tracking modes:
  * --agent-id N   stops early if agent dies (caught, starved, or
                   hazard); stable identity across lifetime
  * --slot K       follows a fixed physics body, continuing through
                   death + rebirth (useful for slot-level analysis)

Writes .npz + .summary.json. Smoke-tested on a step-0 checkpoint:
501-step predator trace runs cleanly, produces 26 KB compressed,
summary shows energy rising from 100 to 144 and 11 global catches
across the window.
commits.author: Axel Browne
